opps.title: Metro Liquor (Linden) — down 29%, your #4 account
opps.body: Still ordering, but 557 cases lighter than last year (29%). It is your #4 account and 4.2% of your commission, so the slide is worth about $557 in modeled commission. The drop is concentrated in Krusovice (-234 cases), Pabst Blue Ribbon (-87 cases) — a mix problem you can work on the next visit, not a lost account.

opps.title: 6 accounts stopped ordering — $350 of commission gone quiet
opps.body: Each of these bought from you last year and has ordered nothing at all in 2026. A lost account is the most expensive kind of decline: there is no brand mix to fix and nothing replaces it automatically — the whole relationship has stopped. The largest, Wine Library, was worth 156 cases last year on its own. These are the calls with the shortest path back to commission, because the account already knows you.

opps.title: Colt 45 — 9% of your commission, down 19% YoY
opps.body: Sales are down 711 cases (19%) vs last year, but Colt 45 is still 9.0% of your total commission — your #3 brand. That decline has already cost about $711 in modeled commission, and recovering half of it is worth roughly $356. 25 accounts bought it last year; 24 have this year — 1 accounts stopped carrying it.

opps.title: 8 accounts holding all year but soft this month — 451 cases behind
opps.body: Year to date each of these is fine, so the relationship is not the problem — but month to date they are all well behind where they were last August. That is the pattern that becomes a bad quarter if nobody catches it, and it is the cheapest kind to fix: the account is still buying, it just has not placed its usual order yet. Together they are 451 cases and about $451 of commission behind last August's pace, with days left in the month to close it.

opps.title: 2 brands with real placement gaps — 22 open doors
opps.body: These brands land in far more accounts like yours than they do in your book. The comparison is not raw company share: it weights each brand's on- and off-premise placement rate by your own channel mix, so an on-premise book is never judged against a supermarket brand's reach. Each door below is valued at what a typical account doing business in that brand actually buys company-wide (the median, not an average), scaled down to the size of the doors you actually call on — so these are ordinary placements in YOUR kind of account, not best-case ones in someone else's. Closing every gap would be worth roughly $63 — that is a ceiling, not a forecast, and it compares against $33,325 of commission in your book today. Take the top one or two lines; the whole list is not a year's work.
